Where this week's projections come from

Each player's number blends, where he has one from each:

  • our model and ESPN's projection, 56% and 44%, measured on 519 graded games;

Each weight is the one that would have been most accurate on this season's finished games, pulled toward its starting value until enough are graded. Waiver moves, by title odds

Each pickup is priced in P(win the title) on the same simulated seasons: claiming now, against waiting and claiming only if he breaks out (you win that claim when your priority beats the other managers who also want him), less what your waiver priority is worth on future claims. Passing is not free: if he breaks out, a rival claims him, and what that does to your title odds is counted. Each move is priced on its own; make one, then refresh. Assumes about a third of active managers chase any one breakout.

Waiver plans: several moves together

Moves interact -- two backs chasing one lineup spot are worth less together, two dead roster spots turned into a starter and his handcuff can be worth more -- so every combination of two or three pickups and drops is screened, and the best priced in title odds against standing pat and against the best single move. Make the plan when it beats that single move by more than the simulation noise; a close call when by less.

Where this week's projections come from

Each player's number blends, where he has one from each:

  • our model and Yahoo's projection, 54% and 46%, measured on 236 graded games;
  • the betting market's implied points, 22% where books priced him (less when only one or two did; 6 of your 13 players this week), measured on 482 graded games;
  • the FantasyPros consensus projection, 15% (9 of your 13 players), measured on 286 graded games.

Each weight is the one that would have been most accurate on this season's finished games, pulled toward its starting value until enough are graded. The same numbers set the lineup, P(win), this week's pickups and streams, and this week's part of every title-odds number on the page: waiver adds and drops, trades, the roster. Season values move 25% of the way toward the FantasyPros rest-of-season consensus (measured on 252 graded games), and every season-long number uses them.

Waiver moves, by title odds

Each pickup is priced in P(win the title) on the same simulated seasons: claiming now, against waiting and claiming only if he breaks out (you win that claim when your priority beats the other managers who also want him), less what your waiver priority is worth on future claims. Passing is not free: if he breaks out, a rival claims him, and what that does to your title odds is counted. Each move is priced on its own; make one, then refresh. Assumes about a third of active managers chase any one breakout.

Waiver plans: several moves together

Moves interact -- two backs chasing one lineup spot are worth less together, two dead roster spots turned into a starter and his handcuff can be worth more -- so every combination of two or three pickups and drops is screened, and the best priced in title odds against standing pat and against the best single move. Make the plan when it beats that single move by more than the simulation noise; a close call when by less.
